correctness.rationale: The Euclidean distance expansion near the 120-degree Fermat vertex separates r-u ~v²/(2u), the small radial quadratic k u² (k=3(1/b+1/c)/8), and angular perturbation β λ sqrt(t)u (β=√3/2). The positive smooth-distance quadratic remainder plus the triangle wedge bound force u=O(sqrt(t)), v=O(t^(3/4)) for bounded-scaled-excess points; hence the limit Gλ=kx²+βλx+y²/(2x) and moving minimum mλ=-β²max(-λ,0)²/(4k). Zero boundary area and common scaled compact containment prove L1/total-variation convergence and t^(5/4) volume Jacobian, not just a pointwise formal expansion. Independent Beta-function and direct cross-section quadrature at b=c=1 give V0=1.68196397526220, Δ0=√3/4, V0/Δ0=3.88432941553954. The independent volume check is not a proof of uniform convergence. All small-t assertions are fixed finite λ; large-|λ| describes the limiting profile only.
